title: Total boundary naturality for a prescribed horseshoe
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $T=(F_1\to F_2\to F_3)$ a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves. Let $I_j$ be injective resolutions of $F_j$, and let $\alpha:I_1\to I_2$, $\beta:I_2\to I_3$ commute with their augmentations and satisfy $\alpha\beta=0$. Assume the resolution sequence is short exact in every degree. Let $S$ be its image under global sections, and assume $S$ is short exact. For an arbitrary family $U_i$ of opens indexed by a type of the same universe as $X$, suppose $T.g$ is surjective on every intersection indexed by a tuple $\mathrm{Fin}(k+1)\to\iota$. For every $q\in\mathbb N$, there is a map $\delta:H^q(\operatorname{Tot}(\check C(U,I_3)))\to H^{q+1}(\operatorname{Tot}(\check C(U,I_1)))$ such that $\delta_{\check C}H(\beta_1)=H(\beta_3)\delta$ and $\delta_SH(\alpha_1)=H(\alpha_3)\delta$. The sections, total complexes and augmentation maps are those of [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction], and the connecting maps are those of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. No Ext identification or covering condition is assumed.

proof.text: Split each degreewise resolution row by injectivity of its first term. The Cech cochain functor is additive, so the displayed splitting equations remain true after applying it and evaluating in each Cech degree. Flipping gives a degreewise short exact sequence of double complexes.

In total degree n, evaluate along the finite set of pairs (p,q) with p+q=n and take its finite coproduct. In AddCommGrpCat this exact functor takes the double-complex short exact sequence to a short exact sequence. The resulting maps are definitionally the total maps. Degreewise detection gives a short exact sequence V of total complexes; let delta be its connecting map.

Prove alpha naturality by the naturality equation for presheaf restriction on each component, followed by the total inclusion equation. Prove beta naturality by evaluating the augmentation equations in degree zero, applying the Cech functor and then using the total inclusion equation. These equations give morphisms from the section and coefficient Cech sequences to V. Apply boundary naturality to each.

theorem abelianCechHorseshoe_total_boundary
    {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (T : ShortComplex (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}))
    (hT : T.ShortExact)
    (I₁ : InjectiveResolution T.X₁) (I₂ : InjectiveResolution T.X₂)
    (I₃ : InjectiveResolution T.X₃)
    (α : I₁.cocomplex ⟶ I₂.cocomplex) (β : I₂.cocomplex ⟶ I₃.cocomplex)
    (hαβ : α ≫ β = 0)
    (hα : I₁.ι ≫ α = (CochainComplex.single₀ _).map T.f ≫ I₂.ι)
    (hβ : I₂.ι ≫ β = (CochainComplex.single₀ _).map T.g ≫ I₃.ι)
    (hrows : ∀ n : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval _ (.up ℕ) n)).ShortExact)
    (hS : ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map
      ((sheafToPresheaf _ _ ⋙ (CategoryTheory.evaluation _ _).obj
        (op (⊤ : X.Opens))).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ))).ShortExact)
    {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hg : ∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → ι),
      Function.Surjective (T.g.hom.app (op (⨅ l, U (y l))))) (q : ℕ) :
    ∃ (δ : ((abelianCechDouble U I₃).total (.up ℕ)).homology q ⟶
        ((abelianCechDouble U I₁).total (.up ℕ)).homology (q + 1)),
      TopCat.Sheaf.cechδ U hT hg q ≫
          HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechBeta U I₁) (q + 1) =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechBeta U I₃) q ≫ δ ∧
      hS.δ q (q + 1) rfl ≫
          HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechAlpha U I₁) (q + 1) =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechAlpha U I₃) q ≫ δ
